ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in an acute-angled $\triangle ABC$, where $\angle A=75^\circ$, $DE$ and $DF$ are the perpendicular bisectors of sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. What is the degree measure of $\angle DBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw DA, DC, \\
since $\angle BAC=75^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle ABC + \angle ACB = 180^\circ - 75^\circ = 105^\circ$, \\
since DE and DF are the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC respectively, \\
thus DA=DB, DA=DC, \\
thus DB=DC, $\angle DBA=\angle DAB$, $\angle DAC=\angle DCA$, \\
thus $\angle DBA+\angle DCA=\angle DAB+\angle DAC=75^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle DBC=\angle DBC= \frac{1}{2} \times (105^\circ - 75^\circ) = \boxed{15^\circ}$, \\

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is located inside the triangle near BC. E is on AB, F is on AC, line segment DE is perpendicular to AB, line segment DF is perpendicular to AC, and the right angles at E and F are also marked in the figure. The problem gives that DE and DF are respectively the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC, and ∠A=75°. Reasoning: Because DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, the distances from D to A and B are equal, that is, DA=DB; because DF is the perpendicular bisector of AC, DA=DC. Therefore DA=DB=DC, and D is the circumcenter of triangle ABC. After connecting DB and DC, ∠BAC=75° is the inscribed angle subtending chord BC, so the central angle ∠BDC subtending the same chord BC is ∠BDC=2×75°=150°. In triangle DBC, DB=DC, so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠DBC=∠BCD=(180°−150°)/2=15°.
